heading: Slot descriptor
text:
### Slot descriptor [IDAT.5.3]

One descriptor describes one slot: what it is called, what type it holds, and
whatever markers its declaration attached to it. A schema's descriptors sit in
an array in declaration order, and a slot's **index in that array is its
identity** -- the name map ([IDAT.5.1]) exists to get from a name to an index,
and every value tuple is positional against the same order ([NFCT.2.1]).

The type set is closed, and one member differs in kind from the rest: a slot
holding a reference to another schema has to say *which*, so the schema
reference is populated **exactly when** the type is the schema type. The
compiler writes no other shape, and a load does not judge it ([IDAT.5.5]).

Everything else is a per-slot marker carried through from the declaration.
Tolerance is the one with a subtlety of its own ([IDAT.5.4]).

`ds_slot_desc_t` and `ds_slot_type_t` are declared in `runtime/include/libds.h`.
